Scale AI defends human expertise in 'The Humans Stay' campaign
posts.body: Scale AI is making its first major brand statement with “The Humans Stay,” a campaign arguing that artificial intelligence still depends on human expertise rather than replacing it. The effort includes a full-page New York Times ad, billboards across New York and San Francisco and a large digital placement in Times Square, all centered on the message that reliable AI cannot exist without human intelligence. Positioning itself against tech narratives that focus on automation and replacement, Scale says its technology is designed to enhance professionals such as analysts, surgeons and soldiers rather than eliminate them. The campaign launches Tuesday with a $1 million media spend and will expand through the summer, including placements timed to NY Tech Week.

posts.title: The Shrinking SERP / AI and the future of Search
offsite content increases brand visibility in AI search and overviews
posts.body: Key takeaways: ◦ *AI-powered search shifts affiliate value from clicks to citations*, making offsite content a core driver of brand visibility and consideration before traffic ever lands. ◦ *Fewer, higher-authority partners consistently outperform large affiliate rosters,* with trusted sources driving disproportionate AI citations and faster visibility gains. ◦ *Content optimized for AI prioritizes answer-first structures*, *quantified comparisons, and real experience* over promotional language or keyword-driven SEO tactics. ◦ *Terminology consistency across brand, partner, and documentation content* materially affects how accurately AI systems describe and recommend your product. ◦ *Early investment in authoritative offsite content compounds over time*, creating default-recommendation status that becomes increasingly difficult for competitors to displace.

posts.body: As creative processes become faster and more automated, *the role of the designer is evolving. Meaning increasingly emerges not only from outcomes, but from the way problems are framed, processes are shaped, and futures are imagined.* The growing relevance of community-driven innovation and cross-disciplinary collaboration reflects a desire to move beyond standardization. The ability to navigate between technological possibility, social reality, and ecological necessity has become a central design competence.
